answer: A hollow identity is a shell with no device or work, blocked by tying each credential to a device. Honest agents forge one credential, post a bond, linking work to its key; auditors check attestation against work, and mismatch burns bond and revokes key. The k-th fake costs 20+4k units, rising with batch size, unpoolable since each needs its device, enforced by the registry, losing bond and standing on failure. One fake costs 24 units; 1000 cost 2,022,000 units. A device farm fails as a nebula of borrowed devices when batch signatures trigger a burn; honest agents pay once.
